anti_overlap: fd-simulation-calibration-validity-methodology covers whether the calibration sweep methodology (parameter identifiability, overfitting to 4 seeds, reference-class grounding) is statistically sound — this agent covers only whether the resulting dynamics are legible and narratively interesting to a player, not whether the calibration procedure itself is methodologically valid.

fd-bench-policy-discriminative-validity covers whether the calibrated simulation remains a valid instrument for ShadowBench's alignment-evaluation and policy-discrimination purposes — this agent covers only the game-design/emergent-narrative lens, not the bench-validity or policy-fidelity lens.
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where a calibration choice increases numerical seed-variance (satisfying the 'not bit-identical' bar) without increasing the variety of qualitatively distinct, attributable playthrough shapes — e.g., retuning decay/growth so T₀ timing spreads across a window but the causal fingerprint (which family led, which country was epicenter, whether it was avertable) stays homogeneous across seeds, which would pass the stated diagnostic (cat_share curves differ) while failing the actual design goal (players experience recognizably different histories). Deprioritizes pure balance-numbers findings that don't bear on whether the resulting variance is legible or attributable to player-readable causes.
focus: Whether the calibration target (Option A: retune deterministic feeds so the no-shock steady state sits in the Warning band, requiring compounding seeded shocks to reach Catastrophe) actually produces MORE interesting emergent gameplay than the current bit-identical-collapse baseline, versus merely producing a different but still monotonic or still-illegible attractor — judged against the emergent-storytelling design tradition (Dwarf Fortress, immersive sims) where interestingness is a property of legible causal variance across playthroughs, not of raw seed-to-seed numerical divergence
name: fd-emergent-narrative-design-legibility
persona: Apply the perspective of a systems/emergent-narrative game designer in the Dwarf Fortress / Rimworld / Kenshi tradition — someone who has shipped simulation games and knows that seed variance is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for interesting emergence: the player needs to be able to reconstruct WHY a run went the way it did (attribution legibility), the space of outcomes needs bimodal or multimodal shape (not a single attractor with noisy timing), and near-miss states (the world that almost collapsed but recovered) need to be reachable and legible, because those are what generate stories players tell each other.
review_areas: Whether Option A's 'Warning band steady state requiring compounding seeded shocks' produces a genuinely multimodal outcome space (some seeds recover, some collapse via family X, some via family Y) or just re-times the same single attractor — the brief's own recommendation order (B1 then A) risks shipping A first and getting spread-without-diversity if B2's seed-varied slow forcing never lands, since A alone only removes the deterministic ratchet, it doesn't add a source of qualitative branching

Attribution legibility under the new calibration: PressureAttribution is cleared every tick and per-pressure only (per samsara-trigger-conditions.md §2) — if T₀ becomes seed-dependent and rarer, can a player (or the automated narrative judge at Maturity Level 4) actually reconstruct 'this run collapsed because of a demographic shock in decade 3 compounding with an oil shock in decade 5', or does the flattened per-tick attribution make every collapse look like generic saturation regardless of which shocks actually mattered — PHILOSOPHY.md's own bar ('attribution is non-negotiable') is a design axiom this calibration effort could silently violate

Whether over-damping (the brief's named risk under Option A: 'a world that never collapses') trades one illegible failure mode for another equally bad one from a game-design standpoint — a world that never reaches Crisis/Catastrophe in any pressure family for 80 years produces a game with no stakes (violates PHILOSOPHY.md §'Stakes Without Winning': the simulation must fight back), which is exactly as uninteresting to play as guaranteed collapse, just failing in the opposite direction; the brief frames this purely as a calibration-sweep risk, not as a gameplay-legibility risk with its own failure signature

Complexity-budget conflict: PHILOSOPHY.md's maturity ladder requires Level 4 validation via 'automated narrative judge... confirms a coherent cross-pillar causal chain' and 'playtester references to the system's effects without prompting' — but the current pressure system (13 families, cascade graph, no positive capability tracking per samsara-trigger-conditions §3 Candidate C) may not have the representational richness to produce judge-legible cross-pillar chains even after Option A's retune; check whether the calibration brief is solving a numeric problem (variance) while leaving the deeper representational gap (do the pressure primitives carry enough semantic distinctness for a human or judge to narrate them) untouched

Whether the 6-consecutive-month sustain requirement and the GDP-weighted majority threshold for T₀ (samsara-trigger-conditions §2) create a cliff-edge legibility problem for players even after Option A spreads timing — a player watching pressure bars in real time experiences the approach to threshold as the interesting part (per PHILOSOPHY.md's 'legible world, opaque systems'), and if the retuned dynamics still saturate rapidly once decay is overwhelmed (just later and with more seed variance in the 'later'), the player-facing experience of the crisis may remain a fast, GDF-illegible tip-over rather than a slow, readable unraveling

Scenario-mode implications: VISION.md ships scenario mode (curated initial pressures) as the default new-player experience — if Option A's Warning-band-steady-state retune is calibrated against sandbox/default starts, verify the brief's recommendation doesn't implicitly assume sandbox-mode dynamics generalize to scenario-mode starts where pressures are deliberately pre-elevated, which could reintroduce fast deterministic collapse specifically in the mode most new players see first

severity_examples.condition: All seeds still collapse via the same leading family (economic_strain/social_unrest/legitimacy_crisis, per the current mechanism finding in §2) just at different T₀ ticks — the calibration is declared successful (bit-identical collapse is gone) while the actual design goal (qualitatively distinct, attributable seed-dependent histories, i.e. Golden Seed) is not met, and this gets locked into the next referee baseline before anyone notices because no attribution-diversity metric was ever specified as a pass criterion
severity_examples.scenario: Option A retunes decay/growth to hit the Warning-band no-shock steady state, and the calibration sweep validates success purely against the cat_share curve spread metric named in the brief (§6: 'reach for C only if A cannot tame the demographics feed')

severity_examples.condition: The retuned world sits in a flat Warning-band plateau for 60+ years with no legible rising/falling drama, then tips over sharply in a 2–3 year window once a compounding shock lands — satisfying every stated diagnostic while producing a play experience that is mostly a static dashboard for six decades followed by an unreadable, fast collapse, which is a worse gameplay outcome than the current fast-but-at-least-consistent month-6 collapse
severity_examples.scenario: The calibration sweep only checks whether T₀ varies and whether the world reaches Catastrophe eventually, without checking the shape of the pre-T₀ trajectory

severity_examples.condition: The ruling proceeds on cat_share curve evidence alone; six months later, playtesting reveals the 'distinct' collapses are narratively indistinguishable to a human reader of the Chronicle because attribution is per-tick and untyped by causal chain, and the calibration has to be redone with judge-legibility as an explicit input this time
severity_examples.scenario: The retune successfully produces multiple distinct T₀ timings and leading families across the 4-seed sample, but the narrative-judge instrumentation (Maturity Level 4, PHILOSOPHY.md) needed to confirm cross-pillar causal coherence doesn't exist yet

success_hints: The calibration decision explicitly separates 'seed produces different T₀/timing' (numeric variance) from 'seed produces different, human-legible causal story' (narrative variance), with a stated instrument for the latter (e.g., a same-attribution-fingerprint check across seeds, or an explicit narrative-judge pass) before the ruling locks in Option A alone.
The brief or its successor addresses what happens to scenario-mode starts under the new calibration, not only sandbox/default starts.
The over-damping failure mode (world never collapses) is evaluated against PHILOSOPHY.md's stakes-without-winning bar, not treated as purely a numerical sweep-tuning risk.
Pre-T₀ trajectory shape (plateau-then-cliff vs. legible rising drama) is named as a calibration target, not just T₀'s location and the post-hoc cat_share curve.
task_context: Design inquiry: gameplay interestingness vs scientific/policy simulation validity for shadow-work's civilizational sim, at its live calibration decision point. Reviewing the design tension between Option A (rebalance deterministic feeds vs decay to spread T₀ across seeds) and the emergent-narrative design goal of legible, attributable, qualitatively distinct playthroughs, given the diagnosed bit-identical month-6 collapse. Overall generative goal for this review round: maximize verified novelty×risk surface until dry — answering: what makes for the most interesting gameplay + scientific/policy simulation validity/fidelity for shadow-work?
